description.narrative: "Objectives:.(1) Relying on partners and local government, NGOs and researchers, develop and implement an executive study tour to Costa Rica in 2013. .(2) In field based settings, teach Congressional Staff and other U.S. Decision-makers about: conservation challenges and solutions, national, regional, and international priorities and related laws/treaties. .(3) Integrate needs and conservation work of local institutions and communities into educational programs, and potentially catalyze conservation activities. .(4) Use networking opportunities between U.S. and host government officials to forge lasting relationships that nurture new conservation policies and investments..The recipient agrees to coordinate with the FWS program officer to: conduct course planning activities, develop course content, and identify project sites and expert speakers. In addition, the ICCF will work closely with the FWS program officer and other FWS staff on project monitoring, evaluation, and follow-up outreach activities as identified in the proposal. Finally, the ICCF will notify the FWS in advance of any changes in lead project staff identified in the proposal..FWS involvement will consist of: (1) working closely with the ICCF to determine course content and methodology, (2) providing guidance for site visits within Costa Rica, and (3) helping to coordinate guest speakers from Wildlife Without Borders-Latin America and Caribbean program partner organizations and institutions. The FWS will approve in advance all topics and subject matter to be covered, sites to be visited, and participating instructors and guest speakers. Up to 3 FWS staff will attend the course at no cost to the ICCF. .Pending availability of funds in FY 2014 and satisfactory project performance, FWS anticipates supplying additional funding to this cooperative agreement to implement an executive study tour in Costa Rica again in 2014. ."
